headline: US Consumer Sentiment Drops Toward Record Low on Rising Fuel Costs
summary: US consumer sentiment fell close to a record low in October as rising fuel prices linked to Middle East conflict and persistent cost-of-living concerns dampened household expectations for the economy.
why: Consumer sentiment is a key leading indicator of US personal consumption expenditures, which account for over two-thirds of US GDP.

impacts.name: US Consumer Discretionary
impacts.why: Weakening sentiment and higher expenditure on necessary fuel depress discretionary retail and leisure spending.
